title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers deployed AI-generated video and social media profiles to impersonate a real immigration attorney and solicit payments from immigrants for fraudulent legal services. The system was an impersonation scheme, operating entirely outside the conditions under which any legitimate legal service exists, with hundreds of fake accounts generating false testimonials and directing victims to payment platforms. Detection occurred only when potential clients contacted the real attorney's office, meaning the fraud went undetected for three months before discovery.

The deployment points to a failure in platform moderation at scale. Social media sites hosted thousands of fraudulent accounts across multiple services, each one verifiable as fake through basic checks against the attorney's real profiles and professional records. An anti-piracy company eventually removed nearly 6,500 accounts, but this happened after victims had already paid for nonexistent services through consumer payment apps.

It is not established how much money was stolen, what specific AI tools generated the videos, or whether the platforms were notified before or after the removals began.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of artificial intelligence scammers who are using fake videos and social media profiles with his likeness to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The scammers created hundreds of AI-generated videos showing Leal offering immigration services such as US residency assistance for $2,200, along with false testimonials from supposed former clients. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and the situation has escalated dramatically over the past three months.

To combat the fraud, Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake social media profiles across multiple platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The scams typically direct victims to WhatsApp, where fraudsters exchange phony contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate. He warns immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to avoid those requesting immediate payment.
